'''Card layout''' shows where to find the gameplay information on a [[Star Wars CCG]] card. Decipher's rulebook identifies the printed fields, and its Glossary explains how the values are used.<ref name="rb20">[[Media:Decipher Rulebook 2.0.pdf|Star Wars Customizable Card Game Rulebook, Version 2.0]], Decipher (November 1998), pp. 4–9 and 13. [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game RULEBOOK 2.0|Wiki transcription]].</ref><ref name="gl20">[[Media:Decipher Glossary 1998.pdf|Star Wars Customizable Card Game Glossary, Version 2.0]], Decipher (November 1998), pp. 2, 20–23, 33–34, 47–49, 61–64, 70, 82, 88, 102 and 134–135. [[Decipher Glossary 2.0|Wiki transcription]].</ref>

== Title and uniqueness ==
Dots before a card title mark it as unique (•) or restricted (••, ••• and so on). The dot count limits how many copies can be on the table and how many can be played or deployed each turn, even if canceled. The number of diamonds (◊) limits the total copies both players may have on the table at each system.<ref name="gl20" /> See [[Uniqueness]] and [[Persona]].

== Card type ==
The icon in the upper-left corner shows the [[Card Type|card type]]. Sites, systems and sectors share the location type and have no upper-left icon.<ref name="gl20" />

== Destiny ==
The destiny number is in the upper-right corner. To draw destiny, reveal the top card of your Reserve Deck, use its destiny value, then place the card face down on your Used Pile. Locations count as destiny zero.<ref name="rb20" /><ref name="gl20" />

== Deploy cost ==
Characters, vehicles and starships show their deploy cost in a small white box. This is the printed amount of Force needed to deploy the card. A card that deploys without a printed or assigned Force cost deploys for free, subject to its other requirements.<ref name="rb20" /><ref name="gl20" />

== Forfeit ==
The small black box shows the forfeit value. It measures how much attrition or battle damage the card can satisfy when forfeited in a battle.<ref name="rb20" /><ref name="gl20" />

== Power ==
Power represents the strength of a character, vehicle or starship. The side with the higher total power wins a battle. Battle destiny can add to that total.<ref name="rb20" /><ref name="gl20" />

== Ability ==
Ability represents a card's capacity to use the Force. It contributes to presence and, in battle, normally permits a battle destiny draw when your participating ability totals four or more. A character uses its ability as its defense value unless its armor is higher. An unarmored droid has defense value zero. Vehicles and starships use their armor or maneuver.<ref name="rb20" /><ref name="gl20" />

== Movement and other attributes ==
Characters have landspeed one by default. Landspeed measures movement between adjacent sites. Hyperspeed measures how far a qualifying starship can move in parsecs.<ref name="gl20" />

== Icons ==
Locations use blue lightsabers for the Light Side and red lightsabers for the Dark Side. These icons determine the location's contribution to Force generation and the base [[Force drain]]. Cards may also show skill icons such as pilot and warrior. The [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game RULEBOOK 2.0#Icon guide|rulebook's icon guide]] identifies card types, skills, sets and location symbols.<ref name="rb20" /><ref name="gl20" />

== Lore ==
Lore gives background about the subject of a card. Some words in lore matter to gameplay, and some are printed in bold.<ref name="gl20" />

== Game text ==
Game text is the large rules text block at the bottom of most cards or on each side of a location. When a card's game text is canceled, other fields such as power, forfeit, lore and icons still apply unless the canceled text defined or affected them.<ref name="gl20" />
